full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: The instant leave petition under Article 103 of the Constitution arises out of the judgment and order dated 28.10.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4069 of 2004 discharging the Rule, Which arose out of the judgment and order dated 3.6.2004 passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat, allowing the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 38 of 1999 setting aside the judgment and order dated 30.05.1999 passed by the Assistant Judge, Rampal, Bagerhat, dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1998 tiled for restoration of Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 after setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 7.5.1997. 

 3. The plaintiffs filed the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 for declaration of title and recovery of possession and on the date (7.5.1997) fixed for ex-parte hearing of the suit, the defendants of the suit did not appear, and accordingly the suit was heard ex-parte and being proved decreed. Thereafter, on 22.01.1998 the defendant Nos. 24 and 25 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1998 under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 after setting aside the ex-parte decree passed on 7.5.1997. 

 4. The trial Court on consideration of the materials on record and submissions of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties dismissed the case and being aggrieved there against the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 38 and 1999 was preferred before the District Judge, Bagerhat, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat, who allowed the appeal vide judgment and order dated 3.6.2004, there by allowed the miscellaneous case and restored the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 7.5.1997. 

 7. It appears that the Title Suit No. 103 of 4989 was decreed ex-parte on 7.5.1997 and the defendant-petitioners of the miscellaneous case contested the suit by filing written statement and they claim to have no knowledge about the ex-parte decree tilt 12.09.1998, on which date the said defendant-petitioners having come to Court to file written statement in Title Suit No. 111 of 1997 enquired about the fate of the Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 and came to know about the ex-parte disposal of the Title Suit 103 of 1989. But while giving deposition in the miscellaneous case the P.W.1 on behalf of the petitioners categorically stated that."I have no other suit in the civil Court  except this suit. I am none of the T.S. No. 111 of 1997. I did not file hajira in T.S. No. 111 of 1997". He further deposed to effect that "no date was fixed for any step on 12.1.98 in T.S. No. 111 of 1997". 

 9. It appears that in disposing of the appeal the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat, observed that the defendant-appellants were interested in the suit for which they have filed the written statement in Title Suit No. 103 of 1989. But due to political rivalry they remained in custody for a long time and hence could not pursue their case in Court and the same was treated as sufficient cause. Further the Appellate Court relying on the provisions of Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure allowed the appeal awarding compensation costs. 

 "I. For that the High Court Division has failed to consider that the appellate Court below is wrong to find that the Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1998 preferred by the defendant Nos. 24 and 25 as petitioners from the judgment and order of ex-parte decree dated 07.05.1997 in Title Suit No. 103 of 1989, is barred by limitation as the date of knowledge of the petitioner on 12.01.1998 is totally false; 

 II. For that the High Court Division has failed to consider that the trail Court after properly considering oral and documentary evidence on record both oral and documentary rightly dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No.3 of 1998 of the defendant (present respondent Nos. 1 and 2) but the Court of appeal below without properly considering the same and without reversing the findings of the trial Court committed error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal and allowing, the said miscellaneous case of the defendant (present, respondent Nos. 1 and 2); 

 III. For that the P.W. 1 Sheikh Motahar Hossain in his examination deposition stated that while on 12.01.1998 he came to the Court for filing written statement in another Title Suit. No. 111 of 1997 he came to learn about the fact of ex-parte decretal of Title Suit No. 103 of 1989, but in his cross-examination he has stated that he had no bother suit except said Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 and that he is neither a tadbirkar of the said another Title Suit No. 111 of 1997 nor date of the said case was fixed on 12.01.1998 in the miscellaneous petition he stated that he had learnt of the disputed ex-parte decree of Title Suit No. 103 of 1989 on 12.01.1998 but the Court of appeal below without considering the same committed an error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal and allowing the miscellaneous case."
